newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon up on tax merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon up on tax merger plan.

text.p: Shares of microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor surged in early Friday trade after the cabinet on Thursday approved a tax merger plan to boost the island's investment and economy, brokers said.

* The cabinet agreed to merge the island's two income taxes into one business income tax and set the merged rate at 25 percent, seen effective from 1998. The move would avoid double taxation and help corporate structures, officials said.
* After 50 minutes at 0150 GMT, Taiwan Semicon was up T$7.5 or 5.27 percent to T$150. Glass giant Taiwan Glass rose the daily seven percent limit to T$48.2.

* The merger would reduce tax revenues by about T$30-40 billion a year, but the finance ministry would recoup the sharp downturn by assessing a 10 percent levy on profits that enterprises reserve rather than distribute to shareholders immeditely, officials said.
* Brokers said the planned 10 percent levy on companies' retained earnings will force those with high retained earnings to issue higher stock dividends in 1998 to avoid double taxation.

* Michael Hung, independent analyst: "If parliament approves the proposal, companies with high retained earnings like Taiwan Semiconductor are expected to issue higher stock dividends in 1998 to avoid double taxation, a move that will benefit general investors."
